text:
Running a 3B parameter model on a smartphone sounds incredible until you watch the battery icon drop 1% every ninety seconds.

Everyone talks about on-device AI privacy, but almost nobody talks about thermal limits.

When testing local inference runtimes on mobile recently, the initial performance numbers looked fantastic on paper. Low latency, zero network roundtrips, total offline privacy. But running continuous local matrix math turns the phone's processor into a pocket warmer fast 📱

Mobile chips are optimized for intense, ultra-short bursts of work — like rendering a 60fps transition or applying a photo filter. Small language models do the exact opposite. They demand steady, high-power calculations for tens of seconds at a time.

Within two minutes, the operating system steps in to save the device from overheating. It throttles the chip frequency down hard ⚡

That smooth, fast token generation suddenly stutters, and your private on-device model becomes significantly slower than a standard cloud API call over a weak cellular network.

The engineering challenge for mobile AI isn't just compressing models down to fit in memory. It's building UI patterns and task workflows designed for two-second bursts of inference rather than long continuous generation.

Are you seeing real user demand for fully offline local AI features, or is a hybrid cloud approach still the only practical answer for longer interactions?
